policies.description: Only users with a role that has Delete permission on all tables may invoke delete_notifications. The Administrator role has full CRUD on all tables, while Manager and Agent roles do not have Delete rights on non‑operational tables such as notifications.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.
Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables.

policies.description: The notification to be deleted must belong to the caller’s organization before the delete operation is performed.
references: Knowledge Scope: Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.

policies.description: Execute delete_notifications as a single validated operation; do not combine it with other actions unless using an approved batch endpoint.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.policy_name: Do not assume or fabricate IDs
policies.description: The notification_id supplied to delete_notifications must be verified against a trusted source (e.g., a prior lookup) and must not be guessed or fabricated.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: If any of the above policies are violated (e.g., insufficient role, notification outside organization, unverified ID), the operation must be halted and the specific policy reason returned before attempting deletion.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: If the delete_notifications call returns a 403 Forbidden response, the operation must be halted and the permission denial reported to the user, as the user role lacks authority for the deletion.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: If the delete_notifications call returns a 409 Conflict response, the operation must be stopped and the conflict reason reported, indicating a record lock or state conflict.
references: 409 Conflict: Record locking or state conflict.

policies.description: When a rate‑limit error is encountered while invoking delete_notifications, the system must pause and retry the request using an exponential backoff strategy.
references: Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

policies.description: Every invocation of delete_notifications must be recorded in an audit log that includes the timestamp (created_on) and the user_id of the requester.
references: Time Tracking: All work logs must include the timestamp (created_on) and the user_id performing the action.

policies.description: The notification to be deleted must be verified to belong to the same organization as the requester and satisfy database integrity rules before the delete_notifications operation is performed.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.

policies.description: The delete_notifications tool may be invoked directly without asking the user for additional confirmation or permission, provided all other policies are satisfied.
references: You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.

policies.description: The delete_notifications tool requires the mandatory field notification_id. If this field is missing or empty, the operation must be halted and the assistant must respond by stating that the notification_id field is required.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.
User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.
